name: emodin
summary: Anthraquinone from rhubarb, cascara, and other plants with cathartic, anti-inflammatory, and MAPK inhibitory effects. Used medicinally for constipation; long-term use has hepatotoxicity and genotoxicity concerns.
description: Emodin, an anthraquinone from rhubarb, is studied for NF-κB and MAPK pathway activity that may influence inflammatory gene expression and stress responses.
safetyNotes: Anthraquinone laxative-like activity may cause diarrhea, electrolyte shifts, and interaction risks. Avoid chronic high-dose use, pregnancy, kidney disease, and stimulant-laxative stacking.
evidence_grade_explanation: Both evidence signals agree on limited evidence.
evidence_rationale: Strongest recorded design is a meta-analysis, drawn from 1 recorded study, 1 in people.
